basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 17.' and it opens 'Vers. 17. Risit. Non dubitatione, sed gaudio credens promissioni Dei. Unde et filius ejus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 17. Risit. Non dubitatione, sed gaudio credens promissioni Dei. Unde et filius ejus Isaac, id est risus vocatus est. Sara vero postea incredulitate risit, unde et increpari meruit.
